proof_nl: Let x be any real number, and set m = floor(x). By the definition of the floor function, m is an integer and m <= x, and moreover m is the greatest integer with this property. Suppose for contradiction that x >= m + 1. Then m + 1 is also an integer, and m + 1 <= x. This contradicts the maximality of m, since m + 1 > m is an integer still not exceeding x. Therefore x < m + 1. Since m = floor(x), we obtain x < floor(x) + 1. Because x was arbitrary, the statement holds for every real number x.
solver_summary: Use the defining maximality property of floor(x): if m = floor(x), then m is the greatest integer <= x. If x were at least m+1, then m+1 would be an integer <= x, contradicting maximality. Hence x < floor(x)+1 for all real x.
